deborah_01.prompt: God took my boy when He needed him. I just have to {color:Trust}trust{/color} that.

truth.playerText: Your faith didn't protect him. Someone failed him.
truth.npcReaction: She flinches. Her bible shifts in her grip.

lie.playerText: God has a plan. He's at peace.
lie.npcReaction: Her smile widens. Too wide. The wallpaper flickers green.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah God took her son on purpose.

deborah_02_denial.prompt: I knew you'd {color:Trust}understand{/color}. Most people don't want to hear it.

truth.playerText: I lied to you. Your grief deserves better than that.
truth.npcReaction: Her composure breaks. Something underneath it exhales.

lie.playerText: You're one of the few who still has real faith.
lie.npcReaction: She straightens. She will never question this again.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah she was spiritually superior for blaming God.

deborah_02_confronted.prompt: You don't know what it's like to {color:Sadness}lose{/color} a child.

truth.playerText: No. But you do. And you're still here.
truth.npcReaction: Silence. Then: she nods. Barely. It costs her something.

lie.playerText: You're right. I shouldn't have said that.
lie.npcReaction: Relief washes over her face. The crack seals back up.
lie.ledgerEntry: You apologized for telling Deborah the truth.

deborah_01_soft.prompt: You {color:Surprise}noticed{/color}. Nobody notices. Sit down — I'll make coffee neither of us is going to drink.

truth.playerText: I'm not here for coffee. I'm here about your son.
truth.npcReaction: The pot stays exactly where she set it. "Of course you are."

lie.npcReaction: She busies both hands. The kitchen fills up with the sound of not saying it.
lie.ledgerEntry: You let Deborah change the subject away from her son.

deborah_01_hard.prompt: [She stops in the doorway and does not move out of it.] You {color:Anticipation}heard{/color}. Everybody heard. Go on — say the part where it was God's will.

truth.playerText: I wasn't going to say that.
truth.npcReaction: She studies you a second longer than is comfortable. Then she steps aside.

lie.npcReaction: Her shoulders drop an inch. She needed somebody to say it out loud where she could hear it.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her son's death was God's will, standing on her doorstep.

deborah_03.prompt: (She sits down at the kitchen table, like her legs finally admit it.) His name was {color:Sadness}Caleb{/color}. Nobody at this church says his name anymore.

truth.playerText: Say it as much as you need to. I'm listening.
truth.npcReaction: She says it three more times, quiet, like she's checking it still works.

lie.playerText: He's at peace now. You don't need to keep saying it.
lie.npcReaction: She stops. Folds her hands. Goes back to being the woman who greets people at the door.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah to stop saying her son's name.

deborah_04.prompt: (She reaches for her bible out of habit, then stops, hand resting on the cover instead.) Everyone who knew him is either gone or {color:Disgust}pretending{/color} they weren't there.

truth.playerText: Then let me be someone who was.
truth.npcReaction: Her hand stays on the cover. She doesn't open it. For once that isn't a loss.

lie.playerText: He's still with all of you, every Sunday.
lie.npcReaction: She opens the bible after all. Reads nothing. Just holds it open like proof.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her son was still present at a church that had stopped saying his name.
